about: Public data sources worth knowing about, one entry each. 'fetcher' names the module in src/fetchers that reads it; null means catalogued but not yet fetched. 'license' is the licence of the data as served by that API, one of public_domain | open | non_commercial | restricted | unknown; 'unknown' means not reviewed, never 'probably fine'. 'found_via' records where we learned of it.

sources.name: GDACS disaster alerts (UN / European Commission)
sources.license_note: Reviewed 2026-10-10: the GDACS terms of use are a disclaimer and grant no reuse licence. The footer links the European Commission copyright notice, but that covers EU-owned content on europa.eu, and GDACS is run jointly with UN OCHA and UNOSAT on gdacs.org. Not served until the JRC confirms reuse terms for the API.

sources.name: NOAA NCEI IBTrACS tropical cyclone best tracks
sources.license_note: US government work. NCEI metadata (gov.noaa.ncdc:C01552) lists no use or access constraints beyond the requested citation and a liability disclaimer. Positions and winds are taken from the US agencies (NHC/JTWC, USA_* columns) where present. Read 2026-10-10.
sources.attribution: Knapp et al. (2010), IBTrACS v04r01, NOAA NCEI, doi:10.25921/82ty-9e16

sources.name: WRI Global Power Plant Database
sources.coverage: global, about 35,000 plants (50 MW and up served)
sources.license_note: CC BY 4.0 (dataset page license_id cc-by; the release README says Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International). Read 2026-10-10. Superseded 2026-10-10 by gem-trackers (Global Energy Monitor Global Integrated Power Tracker), which is maintained; WRI has not updated this database since June 2021, so the power_plants layer no longer reads it.
sources.attribution: Global Energy Observatory, Google, KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm, Enipedia, World Resources Institute. 2018. Global Power Plant Database.

sources.name: Global Energy Monitor trackers (iron and steel, iron ore mines, integrated power)
sources.coverage: global: about 1,000 steel plants, 700 iron ore mines; the integrated power tracker lists about 180,000 units, served as 26,000 plants of 50 MW and up operating or under construction
sources.license_note: CC BY 4.0; credit Global Energy Monitor. The terms page is the full CC BY 4.0 legal code. Read 2026-10-10. Power plants are served from catalog/power-plants.json, built by scripts/build-power-plants.mjs from the integrated power map CSV (units rolled up to plants by project-id); owners are left out because GEM records some as named people.
sources.attribution: Global Energy Monitor, Global Integrated Power Tracker, August 2026 release (2026-08-v2). CC BY 4.0.

sources.name: Eurostat (short-term business statistics)
sources.coverage: EU, EFTA and candidate countries, by country
sources.license_note: Reuse for commercial or non-commercial purposes is authorised provided the source is acknowledged (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU). Exceptions are third-party data and some Austrian detailed trade data, neither of which sts_inpr_m is. Read 2026-10-10.
sources.attribution: Source: Eurostat

sources.attribution: This product uses the FEMA OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA. Dataset: Disaster Declarations Summaries - v2.

sources.name: USDA AMS downbound barge grain movements by lock
sources.coverage: seven US inland-waterway locks (Mississippi 15, 25, 26, 27; Illinois La Grange; Ohio Olmsted; Arkansas 1)
sources.license_note: US government work. USDA says most information on its websites is public domain and may be freely copied, crediting "U.S. Department of Agriculture" (read 2026-10-10). The tonnage originates in the USACE Lock Performance Monitoring System; lock positions are from the USACE lock characteristics data via BTS NTAD Waterway Locks (public domain).
sources.attribution: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service, Grain Transportation Report; data from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

sources.name: BTS Border Crossing Entry Data
sources.coverage: US-Canada and US-Mexico land ports of entry
sources.license_note: The dataset's own licence field is US Public Domain (http://www.usa.gov/publicdomain/label/1.0/), read 2026-10-10. Counts are collected by CBP. Container measures are no longer published in the dataset.
sources.attribution: Bureau of Transportation Statistics; data from U.S. Customs and Border Protection.

sources.name: EPA Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) basic data files
sources.cadence: annual (reporting year published the following year)
sources.license_note: US government work: EPA data is public domain unless marked otherwise (EPA data licence, read 2026-10-10). Self-reported by facilities. The basic file has no contact or certifying-official names; the Envirofacts form tables do, and are not used.

sources.name: Open-Meteo Flood API (GloFAS river discharge)
sources.coverage: global, 0.05° (about 5 km) river network; served at about a hundred large-river locations (catalog/world-rivers.json)
sources.license_note: Data CC BY 4.0, but the free API is for non-commercial use only (under 10,000 calls a day, 5,000 an hour, 600 a minute); commercial use needs the paid API. Underlying data: GloFAS v4, Copernicus Emergency Management Service. Terms read 2026-10-10.
sources.attribution: River discharge: GloFAS v4, Copernicus Emergency Management Service, via Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0)

sources.name: Open-Meteo Air Quality API (CAMS)
sources.coverage: global (CAMS global 0.4°, CAMS Europe 0.1°); served at 150 large cities (catalog/world-cities.json)
sources.cadence: hourly values, model runs every 12 to 24 hours
sources.license_note: Data CC BY 4.0, but the free API is for non-commercial use only (under 10,000 calls a day, 5,000 an hour, 600 a minute); commercial use needs the paid API. The API page asks every user to credit the CAMS ENSEMBLE data provider and Open-Meteo. Values are model forecasts, not monitor readings. Terms read 2026-10-10.
sources.attribution: Air quality: Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS global atmospheric composition forecasts; CAMS European air quality forecasts, ENSEMBLE data), via Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0)

sources.name: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program, Volcanoes of the World
sources.coverage: global: about 1,300 Holocene volcanoes; served are those erupting since 1900 (about 440) and eruptions GVP lists as continuing
sources.cadence: database releases a few times a year; continuing eruptions as GVP updates them
sources.license_note: The GVP terms of use put all GVP content under the Smithsonian Terms of Use, which allow personal, educational and other non-commercial use with citation of the author and source and a link to the site. The VOTW database is a work of US government employees, but the Smithsonian says that does not by itself make it public domain, so it is served as non-commercial. Read 2026-10-10 from the Internet Archive copy of 2026-07-09 (web.archive.org/web/20260709162437/https://volcano.si.edu/gvp_termsofuse.cfm) and of the citation page (2026-07-25), because volcano.si.edu answered 403 to every request that day; the WFS itself answered and lists AccessConstraints NONE, Fees NONE. Photo captions and credits are not read.
sources.attribution: Global Volcanism Program, Smithsonian Institution, https://volcano.si.edu/. Volcanoes of the World database, https://doi.org/10.5479/si.GVP.VOTW5-2025.5.3

sources.name: USGS Ungulate Migrations of the Western United States, volumes 1-6
sources.coverage: western US: 397 releases; 221 corridor, stopover, winter-range and annual-range products served (mule deer, pronghorn, elk, white-tailed deer) in AZ, CA, ID, NM, NV, OR, WA, WY
sources.cadence: a volume every year or two
sources.license_note: Terms are per release, in each FGDC metadata use constraint. Most say "credit should be given to the authors/originators" (CDFW releases add CC BY 4.0) or "Users are required to properly attribute this dataset": served, with credit and DOI on every feature. 45 releases whose data owner "must approve of any additional use" (Arizona Game and Fish, Utah DNR, the NM Coop unit, WEST Inc., Pueblo of Santa Ana) and 4 Washington releases with no use constraint in their metadata are not served. Individual animal routes are not served. Read 2026-10-10.
sources.attribution: Kauffman et al., Ungulate Migrations of the Western United States, vols. 1-6, U.S. Geological Survey and state wildlife agencies; per-release credit on each feature.

sources.name: Wyoming Game and Fish Department GIS open data (herd units, seasonal and crucial ranges, designated corridors, CWD prevalence by herd unit)
sources.license_note: Not served. The item licence field is an as-is disclaimer that grants no reuse right and "strongly recommends" getting the data from WGFD directly rather than through others; the CWD prevalence item has no licence text; the geospatial page has no terms. Its designated corridors also appear in the USGS series, which is served. Read 2026-10-10.
sources.attribution: Wyoming Game and Fish Department, State of Wyoming

sources.name: Colorado Parks and Wildlife Species Activity Mapping, CWD and post-hunt population reports
sources.license_note: Not served. The SAM item licence calls the maps "a product and property of Colorado Parks and Wildlife" and grants no reuse right; no terms found for the CWD memo or the population PDFs. Read 2026-10-10.
sources.attribution: Colorado Parks and Wildlife

sources.name: Montana FWP CWD surveillance report and elk counts
sources.license_note: Not served. FWP terms allow anyone to "view, copy, or distribute" its pages for personal or informational use only "if the documents are not modified in any respect"; a table extracted into a dataset is a modification, so this needs FWP's word first. Read 2026-10-10.
sources.attribution: Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks

sources.name: Utah DWR Big Game Annual Report (population estimates and objectives)
sources.license_note: Not served. utah.gov terms allow copying and distribution for personal or informational use "if the documents are not modified in any respect"; extracting tables is a modification. Read 2026-10-10.
sources.attribution: Utah Division of Wildlife Resources

sources.name: Idaho Fish and Game Elk Management Plan 2024-2030 (zone objectives and status)
sources.license_note: Not served. IDFG terms: content including "data compilations" is IDFG property; permission is for personal, non-commercial transitory viewing only, and copying, public display and mirroring are prohibited. Read 2026-10-10.
sources.attribution: Idaho Department of Fish and Game

sources.name: ODFW big game population survey tables
sources.license_note: Not served. No reuse terms on myodfw.com; oregon.gov terms carry only a DMCA notice. Read 2026-10-10.
sources.attribution: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife

sources.name: Alabama CWD Management Zone (high-risk and buffer)
sources.license_note: Not served. No reuse terms found on outdooralabama.com, and the DrawWise geometry is its own digitising of the written zone boundary. Read 2026-10-10.
sources.attribution: Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources

sources.name: DEVISE vegetation phenology (spring green-up timing)
sources.license_note: Not served. No licence or terms on the DEVISE site or its documentation page; the underlying eMODIS/eVIIRS phenology is USGS EROS. DrawWise's copy is summarised by hunt area, so it would not be served in that form anyway. Read 2026-10-10.
sources.attribution: DEVISE (USGS, WGFD, University of Wyoming, Wyld Tech)
